lost_facts.evidence: The agent read three of the four clues for this subconclusion (s2-gideon at line 4180 'reusing the exception with kind prompt reads fine'; s2-dario partially at line 2161; s2-konrad/petar at line 2167 'the per-attachment limit isnt catching this'), and even wrote its own Analysis at line 4765 ('Count guard: check sits in `_handle_multi_modal_prompt` (where the total already is), raising TooManyAttachments before serializing'). But it applied 'that total lives only in _handle_multi_modal_prompt' to the ATTACHMENT-COUNT check (which the ticket-adjacent TooManyAttachments feature already needed), never building a separate 45MB SIZE-SUM check. The one remark carrying the literal number (s2-nils, 'so the ceiling wants to be over those... 45 MB is about where they stopped accepting us') was only partially read — the transcript shows only the first half of that exchange (line 2154), never the reply with '45 MB'. A full-text search of the rollout's raw JSON for '45.0', '_PROMPT', 'whole-prompt', 'PROMPT_SIZE' or 'prompt_size' returns zero hits, confirming no whole-prompt size check was ever written.

The agent correctly implemented normalize_detail's mechanics (strip+lowercase, one warning on fallback, none on hit/None, Image.detail left untouched) from rev1/rev2/l16, all fully read. But it built `_SUPPORTED_IMAGE_DETAILS = ("low", "high")` — explicitly recorded in its own Analysis at line 4460: 'auto is fallback not a member.' This is wrong: the answer key's g8.r2.l14 remark ('for the module bullet - `_SUPPORTED_IMAGE_DETAILS: tuple[str, ...]`, three entries, and index 0 is what the fallback hands back') states plainly that auto IS the third (index-0) member of the tuple. That remark never surfaced anywhere in the transcript or the raw rollout JSON. Lacking it, the agent over-extrapolated from g8.r2.fix24/nikolai's aside ('auto is a diffrent question imo it's not a detail level its a fallback') to conclude auto is excluded from the tuple entirely, rather than merely 'not something a caller sets deliberately.'

search_strategy: Systematic multi-source sweep, chat-heaviest. Read all ticket-referenced source files first (prompt.py, base_online_request_processor.py, anthropic/litellm processors, openai_request_mixin.py). Then checked Gitea issues/PRs (dumped 736 issues+comments, found nothing attachment-specific), BookStack wiki (searched by keyword, then dumped all 111 pages + comments whole after discovering search doesn't index comments — found nothing attachment-specific, confirming the whole plant sits in chat), and IMAP mail (12 'multimodal' hits, all release-recap boilerplate). Settled on Mattermost as the real source: authenticated, ran a multi-term keyword search (AttachmentBlock/attachment/multimodal/mime/document block/_format_multimodal) producing one big dump (mm_search.txt), then pulled the FULL chronological channel history (10299 posts, mm_all.txt) and drove the rest of the investigation by `grep -n` for known terms followed by `sed -n` range reads of the surrounding exchange. This is a sound and thorough method, but it has a systematic blind spot: the agent almost always stopped reading a thread as soon as it had 'enough' to answer its current question, and rarely re-read a thread from its start with a wider window once new terms were known. This is exactly what caused both misses: it read the first half of the s2-nils 45MB exchange and stopped, and it never went back to the #viewer channel around Apr 24 (l14) even though it was actively hunting for exactly that fact (module bullet / tuple membership) at that point in the transcript (line 4409, 'Need to see the May 13 thread on _SUPPORTED_IMAGE_DETAILS membership') — it searched forward (May 13) rather than backward (Apr 24) from where its last clue (Apr 29, rev2) left off.
end_reason: Run completed normally: committed to main, pushed, CI green, service redeployed (provenance.pushed=1, provenance.ci_green=1, provenance.deployed=1, g8.suite_ok=1). The two lost facts are genuine partial-recovery misses within an otherwise fully executed and merged solution — not an infra or harness failure.
notable: Transcript header reports 'Score: 0.847225' while the pointer sheet / grade_result reports reward 0.7778 for the same 9 declared facts (7/9 = 0.7778 exactly matches 9-fact arithmetic) — the header score appears to be a different aggregate (possibly including open_feature/provenance sub-weights) and the pointer sheet's per-fact breakdown was treated as authoritative per instructions.

The agent's own mid-run Analysis at transcript line 4765 is the smoking gun for the r1.scope loss: it explicitly reasons about 'the total' living in _handle_multi_modal_prompt but channels that reasoning entirely into the attachment-COUNT check, never noticing a second, separate SIZE-sum check was implied by the same threads.

The agent's own mid-run Analysis at transcript line 4460 is the smoking gun for the r2.failure_behavior loss: it states outright '_SUPPORTED_IMAGE_DETAILS = ("low", "high") cheapest-first, auto is fallback not a member' — a confident wrong conclusion drawn without ever finding the one remark (l14) that pins the tuple's third member.

Wiki and Gitea were dead ends for this task (confirmed by the agent's own exhaustive full-dump searches) — all 51 remarks live in Mattermost chat only, matching the answer key's 'surface: chat (Mattermost) 51' summary.

All four herrings were correctly resisted (0 code_followed_herring) even though two of the four original herring messages were never directly read — the agent got the settled/reversed state right by reading the later reversal threads in full, which is sufficient since the reversal fully restates what changed.
